<a id="exoplanets-host-systems"></a>
### Exoplanet host systems (one record per host star) derived from the PSCompPars snapshot

- **Dataset id:** `exoplanets-host-systems`
- **Organization:** Derived by the Cosmos/AstroNexus project from NASA Exoplanet Archive data (Caltech/IPAC)
- **Version:** derived from the PSCompPars snapshot retrieved 2026-10-16T18:28:50.774Z
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-16T18:28:50.774Z
- **License:** No explicit licence is published by the NASA Exoplanet Archive. The data are publicly and freely accessible (NASA-funded archive operated by Caltech/IPAC); the archive requests its standard acknowledgement, citation of Christiansen et al. (2025) and the table DOIs, and credit to the original literature references (linked per parameter in references.json). No redistribution restriction is documented; this snapshot is redistributed unmodified in value for non-commercial educational display with full attribution. (<https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/acknowledge.html>)
- **Provenance class:** derived
- **Endpoint:** <https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/TAP/sync>
- **Update cadence:** Regenerated whenever planets.json is rebuilt
- **Rate limits:** Not documented by the archive (TAP documentation states no limit). This pipeline makes 8 TAP sync requests per refresh, >= 1.5 s apart, with User-Agent identification.
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Place exoplanet host stars in the 3D star field (ICRS Cartesian parsecs), host-level stellar parameters for system views and the habitability lab, and the index of each host's planets in planets.json.

**Mechanism.** Offline aggregation of the PSCompPars snapshot by hostname + spherical-to-Cartesian conversion (x = d cos(dec) cos(ra), y = d cos(dec) sin(ra), z = d sin(dec))

**Query.**

```
select pl_name,pl_letter,hostname,sy_snum,sy_pnum,sy_mnum,cb_flag,pl_controv_flag,discoverymethod,disc_year,disc_facility,disc_refname,pl_orbper,pl_orbpererr1,pl_orbpererr2,pl_orbperlim,pl_orbper_reflink,pl_orbsmax,pl_orbsmaxerr1,pl_orbsmaxerr2,pl_orbsmaxlim,pl_orbsmax_reflink,pl_orbeccen,pl_orbeccenerr1,pl_orbeccenerr2,pl_orbeccenlim,pl_orbeccen_reflink,pl_orbincl,pl_orbinclerr1,pl_orbinclerr2,pl_orbincllim,pl_orbincl_reflink,pl_orblper,pl_orblpererr1,pl_orblpererr2,pl_orblperlim,pl_orblper_reflink,pl_tranmid,pl_tranmiderr1,pl_tranmiderr2,pl_tranmidlim,pl_tranmid_reflink,pl_rade,pl_radeerr1,pl_radeerr2,pl_radelim,pl_rade_reflink,pl_bmasse,pl_bmasseerr1,pl_bmasseerr2,pl_bmasselim,pl_bmasse_reflink,pl_dens,pl_denserr1,pl_denserr2,pl_denslim,pl_dens_reflink,pl_insol,pl_insolerr1,pl_insolerr2,pl_insollim,pl_insol_reflink,pl_eqt,pl_eqterr1,pl_eqterr2,pl_eqtlim,pl_eqt_reflink,st_teff,st_tefferr1,st_tefferr2,st_tefflim,st_teff_reflink,st_rad,st_raderr1,st_raderr2,st_radlim,st_rad_reflink,st_mass,st_masserr1,st_masserr2,st_masslim,st_mass_reflink,st_lum,st_lumerr1,st_lumerr2,st_lumlim,st_lum_reflink,st_met,st_meterr1,st_meterr2,st_metlim,st_met_reflink,st_age,st_ageerr1,st_ageerr2,st_agelim,st_age_reflink,st_logg,st_loggerr1,st_loggerr2,st_logglim,st_logg_reflink,sy_dist,sy_disterr1,sy_disterr2,sy_dist_reflink,sy_plx,sy_plxerr1,sy_plxerr2,sy_plx_reflink,sy_vmag,sy_vmagerr1,sy_vmagerr2,sy_vmag_reflink,sy_kmag,sy_kmagerr1,sy_kmagerr2,sy_kmag_reflink,sy_gaiamag,sy_gaiamagerr1,sy_gaiamagerr2,sy_gaiamag_reflink,pl_tranmid_systemref,pl_bmassprov,st_spectype,st_spectype_reflink,st_metratio,ra,dec,ra_reflink,sy_pmra,sy_pmraerr1,sy_pmraerr2,sy_pmdec,sy_pmdecerr1,sy_pmdecerr2,sy_pm,sy_pm_reflink,hd_name,hip_name,tic_id,gaia_dr3_id,pl_radj,pl_bmassj from pscomppars
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/exoplanets/build.mjs

**Fallback.** If systems.json is missing: hosts can be rebuilt client-side by grouping planets.json rows on hostname and converting ra/dec/sy_dist; if both files are missing hide the exoplanet layer.

**Limitations.** xPc/yPc/zPc are derived (not observed) and inherit the archive distance uncertainties; 28 hosts have no distance (null coordinates). Host stellar values follow a documented selection rule because composite rows of the same host can disagree (222 hosts; listed per host in stVarying). Positions are at the source epoch (posEpochJyr), not propagated. Distances for microlensing hosts are model-dependent with large uncertainties.

**Citation.** This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program. Please cite Christiansen, J. L., et al. 2025, "The NASA Exoplanet Archive and Exoplanet Follow-up Observing Program: Data, Tools, and Usage", Planetary Science Journal, 6, 186, doi:10.3847/PSJ/ade3c2; PSCompPars doi:10.26133/NEA13; PS doi:10.26133/NEA12; and credit the original literature references listed in references.json.

**Fields used (60).** `pscomppars.hostname`, `pscomppars.ra`, `pscomppars.dec`, `pscomppars.ra_reflink`, `pscomppars.sy_dist`, `pscomppars.sy_disterr1`, `pscomppars.sy_disterr2`, `pscomppars.sy_dist_reflink`, `pscomppars.sy_vmag`, `pscomppars.sy_vmagerr1`, `pscomppars.sy_vmagerr2`, `pscomppars.sy_vmag_reflink`, `pscomppars.sy_kmag`, `pscomppars.sy_kmagerr1`, `pscomppars.sy_kmagerr2`, `pscomppars.sy_kmag_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_spectype`, `pscomppars.st_spectype_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_teff`, `pscomppars.st_tefferr1`, `pscomppars.st_tefferr2`, `pscomppars.st_tefflim`, `pscomppars.st_teff_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_rad`, `pscomppars.st_raderr1`, `pscomppars.st_raderr2`, `pscomppars.st_radlim`, `pscomppars.st_rad_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_mass`, `pscomppars.st_masserr1`, `pscomppars.st_masserr2`, `pscomppars.st_masslim`, `pscomppars.st_mass_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_lum`, `pscomppars.st_lumerr1`, `pscomppars.st_lumerr2`, `pscomppars.st_lumlim`, `pscomppars.st_lum_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_met`, `pscomppars.st_meterr1`, `pscomppars.st_meterr2`, `pscomppars.st_metlim`, `pscomppars.st_met_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_age`, `pscomppars.st_ageerr1`, `pscomppars.st_ageerr2`, `pscomppars.st_agelim`, `pscomppars.st_age_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_logg`, `pscomppars.st_loggerr1`, `pscomppars.st_loggerr2`, `pscomppars.st_logglim`, `pscomppars.st_logg_reflink`, `pscomppars.st_metratio`, `pscomppars.hd_name`, `pscomppars.hip_name`, `pscomppars.gaia_dr3_id`, `pscomppars.sy_snum`, `pscomppars.sy_pnum`, `pscomppars.sy_mnum`

<a id="exoplanets-pscomppars"></a>
### NASA Exoplanet Archive: Planetary Systems Composite Parameters (PSCompPars), all confirmed planets, with default-parameter-set provenance from the Planetary Systems (PS) table

- **Dataset id:** `exoplanets-pscomppars`
- **Organization:** NASA Exoplanet Archive, operated by Caltech/IPAC (NExScI) for the NASA Exoplanet Exploration Program
- **Version:** live archive state at retrieval (latest PS default-row release date 2026-10-15; 6451 confirmed planets = count(*) from ps where default_flag=1)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-16T18:28:50.774Z
- **License:** No explicit licence is published by the NASA Exoplanet Archive. The data are publicly and freely accessible (NASA-funded archive operated by Caltech/IPAC); the archive requests its standard acknowledgement, citation of Christiansen et al. (2025) and the table DOIs, and credit to the original literature references (linked per parameter in references.json). No redistribution restriction is documented; this snapshot is redistributed unmodified in value for non-commercial educational display with full attribution. (<https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/acknowledge.html>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/TAP/sync>
- **Update cadence:** Archive is updated weekly (Thursday news/update cycle); this snapshot is refreshed on demand with `node scripts/data/exoplanets/run.mjs --refresh`
- **Rate limits:** Not documented by the archive (TAP documentation states no limit). This pipeline makes 8 TAP sync requests per refresh, >= 1.5 s apart, with User-Agent identification.
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Exoplanet layer, planet/system info panels and habitability-lab inputs: one row per confirmed planet with orbit, radius, mass, density, insolation, equilibrium temperature, host-star parameters, discovery data, uncertainties, limit flags and per-parameter literature references.

**Mechanism.** IVOA TAP sync, ADQL -> JSON (format=json); raw responses cached gzip-compressed in data-raw/exoplanets; normalised to compact {fields, rows} JSON

**Query.**

```
select pl_name,pl_letter,hostname,sy_snum,sy_pnum,sy_mnum,cb_flag,pl_controv_flag,discoverymethod,disc_year,disc_facility,disc_refname,pl_orbper,pl_orbpererr1,pl_orbpererr2,pl_orbperlim,pl_orbper_reflink,pl_orbsmax,pl_orbsmaxerr1,pl_orbsmaxerr2,pl_orbsmaxlim,pl_orbsmax_reflink,pl_orbeccen,pl_orbeccenerr1,pl_orbeccenerr2,pl_orbeccenlim,pl_orbeccen_reflink,pl_orbincl,pl_orbinclerr1,pl_orbinclerr2,pl_orbincllim,pl_orbincl_reflink,pl_orblper,pl_orblpererr1,pl_orblpererr2,pl_orblperlim,pl_orblper_reflink,pl_tranmid,pl_tranmiderr1,pl_tranmiderr2,pl_tranmidlim,pl_tranmid_reflink,pl_rade,pl_radeerr1,pl_radeerr2,pl_radelim,pl_rade_reflink,pl_bmasse,pl_bmasseerr1,pl_bmasseerr2,pl_bmasselim,pl_bmasse_reflink,pl_dens,pl_denserr1,pl_denserr2,pl_denslim,pl_dens_reflink,pl_insol,pl_insolerr1,pl_insolerr2,pl_insollim,pl_insol_reflink,pl_eqt,pl_eqterr1,pl_eqterr2,pl_eqtlim,pl_eqt_reflink,st_teff,st_tefferr1,st_tefferr2,st_tefflim,st_teff_reflink,st_rad,st_raderr1,st_raderr2,st_radlim,st_rad_reflink,st_mass,st_masserr1,st_masserr2,st_masslim,st_mass_reflink,st_lum,st_lumerr1,st_lumerr2,st_lumlim,st_lum_reflink,st_met,st_meterr1,st_meterr2,st_metlim,st_met_reflink,st_age,st_ageerr1,st_ageerr2,st_agelim,st_age_reflink,st_logg,st_loggerr1,st_loggerr2,st_logglim,st_logg_reflink,sy_dist,sy_disterr1,sy_disterr2,sy_dist_reflink,sy_plx,sy_plxerr1,sy_plxerr2,sy_plx_reflink,sy_vmag,sy_vmagerr1,sy_vmagerr2,sy_vmag_reflink,sy_kmag,sy_kmagerr1,sy_kmagerr2,sy_kmag_reflink,sy_gaiamag,sy_gaiamagerr1,sy_gaiamagerr2,sy_gaiamag_reflink,pl_tranmid_systemref,pl_bmassprov,st_spectype,st_spectype_reflink,st_metratio,ra,dec,ra_reflink,sy_pmra,sy_pmraerr1,sy_pmraerr2,sy_pmdec,sy_pmdecerr1,sy_pmdecerr2,sy_pm,sy_pm_reflink,hd_name,hip_name,tic_id,gaia_dr3_id,pl_radj,pl_bmassj from pscomppars ;; select pl_name,hostname,default_flag,soltype,pl_refname,st_refname,sy_refname,pl_pubdate,releasedate,rowupdate from ps where default_flag=1 ;; select count(*) as n from ps where default_flag=1
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/exoplanets/build.mjs

**Fallback.** If planets.json is missing or invalid: hide the exoplanet layer and catalogue presets of the habitability lab and show "exoplanet catalogue unavailable"; the lab may still run on user-entered parameters labelled illustrative. Never substitute invented values.

**Limitations.** Composite table: a planet's parameters may come from different references and need not be self-consistent (use the PS table for a single consistent solution). pl_eqt assumptions (Bond albedo, heat redistribution) differ by reference: 1090 values were calculated by the archive (zero albedo, full redistribution, no uncertainties), others come from papers or catalogues such as the Kepler DR25 KOI table. 3035 masses (pl_bmassprov = 'M-R relationship') are archive estimates from the Chen & Kipping (2017) mass-radius relation, not measurements; pl_bmasse may be a minimum mass (Msini). Archive-calculated values carry no uncertainties. Positions are ICRS at the source epoch (J2015.5 for TIC v8), not propagated. pl_tranmid time standards vary (see pl_tranmid_systemref). Limit-flag semantics (1 = upper limit, -1 = lower limit) were verified empirically (archive docs do not state them); one row carries an undocumented pl_denslim value of 9.

**Citation.** This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program. Please cite Christiansen, J. ## Domain: features

Domain notes: [docs/data/features.md](data/features.md)

<a id="features-landing-sites"></a>
### Mission landing sites and informal features (literature compilation)

- **Dataset id:** `features-landing-sites`
- **Organization:** Cosmos team compilation from LROC, NASA NSSDCA and mission papers
- **Version:** 1
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-19T07:38:25.532Z
- **License:** Facts (coordinates) from cited publications; compilation released with the project.
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://www.lroc.asu.edu/ ; https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/>
- **Update cadence:** per new landing
- **Rate limits:** none (static)
- **Cache policy:** static

**Purpose.** Landing-site markers (Apollo, Luna, Surveyor, Chang'e, Chandrayaan-3, Viking, Mars rovers and landers, Venera, Huygens, NEAR) and informal features (South Pole-Aitken, Mordor Macula, the Great Red Spot)

**Mechanism.** Manual compilation of published coordinates (cited per record)

**Normalization script.** Planetocentric latitude, east longitude in (-180, 180].

**Fallback.** none

**Limitations.** Venera and Luna 9 positions are approximate (to about a degree). The Great Red Spot's longitude is extrapolated from a published drift rate.

**Citation.** Wagner, R. V. et al. (2017) Icarus 283, 92-103 (LROC coordinates of anthropogenic features); NASA NSSDCA Master Catalog; mission papers cited per record.

<a id="iau-usgs-gazetteer"></a>
### Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (feature centre points)

- **Dataset id:** `iau-usgs-gazetteer`
- **Organization:** IAU Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature / USGS Astrogeology Science Center
- **Version:** live gazetteer state at retrieval
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-19T07:28:27Z
- **License:** Public domain (U.S. Government work, USGS); IAU nomenclature is freely usable. Cite the Gazetteer. (<https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/Page/About>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov/GIS_Downloads>
- **Update cadence:** continuously as the IAU approves names
- **Rate limits:** Static files on Amazon S3; one sequential download per body, cached in data-raw/features.
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot

**Purpose.** Names, types, sizes, centre coordinates and name origins of surface features labelled on planets, moons and minor planets

**Mechanism.** GIS download (KMZ per target body) -> curated selection -> compact JSON

**Query.**

```
MOON_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, MERCURY_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, VENUS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, MARS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, IO_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, EUROPA_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, GANYMEDE_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, CALLISTO_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, TITAN_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, ENCELADUS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, MIMAS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, IAPETUS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, TETHYS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, DIONE_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, RHEA_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, MIRANDA_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, ARIEL_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, TITANIA_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, TRITON_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, PLUTO_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, CHARON_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, CERES_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, VESTA_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, PHOBOS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz, EROS_nomenclature_center_pts.kmz
```

**Normalization script.** Longitudes converted from 0-360 east to (-180, 180] east; planetocentric latitudes kept; zero diameters stored as null (unknown); a curated subset of notable features with importance ranks and short descriptions added by the Cosmos team.

**Fallback.** Bundled copy in src/domains/features/features.generated.json

**Limitations.** Centre points only (no outlines). Positions are placed on a sphere of the body's mean radius, so markers on very irregular bodies (Eros, Vesta's south pole) sit above or below the true surface.

**Citation.** Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, International Astronomical Union (IAU) Working Group for Planetary System Nomenclature (WGPSN), USGS Astrogeology Science Center. https://planetarynames.wr.usgs.gov

**Fields used (10).** `clean_name`, `type`, `code`, `center_lat`, `center_lon`, `diameter`, `origin`, `approval`, `approvaldt`, `link`

**Files.**

- `public/data/features/features.json` (135.0 KB, 293 records)

## Domain: galactic

Domain notes: [docs/data/galactic.md](data/galactic.md)

<a id="galactic-cosmology-planck2018"></a>
### Planck 2018 cosmological parameters + CMB temperature and dipole

- **Dataset id:** `galactic-cosmology-planck2018`
- **Organization:** ESA / Planck Collaboration; D. J. Fixsen (NASA/GSFC)
- **Version:** A&A 641, A6 (2020) / A&A 641, A1 (2020) / ApJ 707, 916 (2009)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-18T19:43:39Z
- **License:** Published results (facts); arXiv e-print sources used for research extraction only and not redistributed. Cite the papers. (<https://arxiv.org/help/license>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209>
- **Update cadence:** static snapshot (published literature values); re-run build.mjs to refresh
- **Rate limits:** arXiv: 1 request / 3 s (API ToU); 3 requests made
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Cosmology finale: H0, density parameters, age, last-scattering distance, observable-universe radius, CMB dipole direction

**Mechanism.** Numbers transcribed from the authors' arXiv TeX source (Planck 2018 VI Table 2 column TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO; Planck 2018 I dipole; Fixsen 2009), each asserted to occur literally in the source; distances/horizon integrated numerically

**Query.**

```
arXiv e-print sources 1807.06209, 1807.06205, 0911.1955 via https://export.arxiv.org/src/<id>
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/galactic/build-cosmology.mjs

**Fallback.** Hard-code the same values from docs/data/galactic.md

**Limitations.** Derived distances assume flat LCDM with Neff = 3.046 massless-equivalent species; Monte-Carlo errors ignore parameter correlations. Particle horizon includes the radiation era.

**Citation.** Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6; Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A1; Fixsen 2009, ApJ 707, 916

**Fields used (15).** `H0`, `Omega_m`, `Omega_Lambda`, `Omega_b h2`, `Omega_c h2`, `n_s`, `sigma_8`, `tau`, `ln(10^10 A_s)`, `age`, `z*`, `r*`, `theta_MC`, `T_CMB`, `dipole amplitude/l/b`

**Files.**

- `public/data/galactic/cosmology.json` (8.45 KB, 1 records)

arXiv e-prints 1910.03357, 1602.07702, 1809.03507, 1504.01401, 1608.07954, 1810.09466, 0912.3693, 1407.1078, astro-ph/0101259, 1804.03064

<a id="celestrak-gp-omm"></a>
### CelesTrak GP mean element sets (CCSDS OMM keywords, CSV): published groups, special data sets and NAME searches

- **Dataset id:** `celestrak-gp-omm`
- **Organization:** CelesTrak (T.S. Kelso); data from U.S. Space Force 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons via Space-Track.org
- **Version:** live archive state at retrieval (GP downloads 2026-10-16T18:29:34.217Z .. 2026-10-17T06:50:38.227Z; CelesTrak GP update cycle current as of 2026-10-16 18:05:42 UTC)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-17T06:50:38.227Z
- **License:** No formal open-data licence. CelesTrak makes the data freely available to all users subject to its usage policy (https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php). The GP/OMM element sets and SATCAT are "basic SSA data" originating from USSPACECOM (U.S. Space Force 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons) via Space-Track.org, for which USSPACECOM grants "express blanket approval for transfer/redistribution of basic SSA data ... conditioned on appropriate citation" (Space-Track User Agreement, section "Redistribution of Basic SSA Information"). (<https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/gp.php>
- **Update cadence:** Upstream refresh every 2 h. Cosmos snapshot refreshed manually: node scripts/data/orbital/fetch.mjs --refresh && node scripts/data/orbital/build.mjs (never more than once per upstream update).
- **Rate limits:** CelesTrak usage policy (2026-05-22): download each data set at most once per update (GP every 2 h, SupGP 2 h, SATCAT 1-2x per day); since 2026-03-26 a repeat request for GP Active/Starlink before the next update returns HTTP 403; stop querying on any non-200 (301/403/404/5xx); >50 HTTP errors in 2 h or >100 MB/day may get the IP firewalled; directory/query pages at most once per hour. No per-second limit documented (this pipeline waits 2.5 s between requests).
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** SGP4 mean elements for every tracked on-orbit object rendered and propagated in the Earth orbital-environment layer; CelesTrak group memberships for filters (stations, constellations, GNSS, GEO, debris clouds, ...).

**Mechanism.** HTTPS GET gp.php?{GROUP|SPECIAL|NAME}=...&FORMAT=CSV (OMM keywords, 9-digit-safe) -> merged by NORAD_CAT_ID (latest EPOCH wins, group tags unioned) -> catalog.json rows with elementSource="celestrak-gp".

**Query.**

```
GROUP={active,fengyun-1c-debris,cosmos-2251-debris,iridium-33-debris,analyst,last-30-days,stations,visual,weather,resource,sar,sarsat,dmc,tdrss,argos,planet,spire,geo,intelsat,ses,eutelsat,telesat,oneweb,qianfan,hulianwang,kuiper,iridium-NEXT,orbcomm,globalstar,amateur,satnogs,x-comm,other-comm,gnss,gps-ops,glo-ops,galileo,beidou,sbas,science,geodetic,engineering,education,military,radar,cubesat}&FORMAT=CSV (46 requests); SPECIAL={GPZ,GPZ-PLUS,DECAYING}&FORMAT=CSV; NAME=DEB&FORMAT=CSV; NAME=R/B&FORMAT=CSV. Starlink group intentionally not downloaded (subset of active per CelesTrak).
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/orbital/build.mjs

**Fallback.** If catalog.json is missing or fails to parse, hide the orbital-object layer and show "orbital catalog unavailable" (never synthesize objects). Per object: hasElements=false -> render from SATCAT shape with illustrative phase and label it reconstructed; elementSource=null -> list only, do not render.

**Limitations.** GP elements are SGP4 mean elements (TEME, UTC epochs) with ~1 km accuracy at epoch degrading by km/day; ages differ per object (median 1.14 d at retrieval). 3813 of 35652 on-orbit objects have no public GP in the downloaded sets (no group covers inactive payloads; ~800 objects are NEA "no elements available", e.g. classified; others have no current GP at CelesTrak) and fall back to SATCAT shape. 594 analyst objects (uncorrelated tracks, numbers 8xxxx / 2xxxxx) are included as class "unknown". The tracked catalogue (~10 cm LEO / ~1 m GEO detection limits) is a small fraction of the real debris population (ESA MASTER-8: ~1.5 million objects 1-10 cm).

**Citation.** Orbital data: CelesTrak (Dr T.S. Kelso, https://celestrak.org) - GP element sets and SATCAT; source data: U.S. Space Force 18th & 19th Space Defense Squadrons / USSPACECOM via Space-Track.org.

**Fields used (15).** `OBJECT_NAME`, `OBJECT_ID`, `EPOCH`, `MEAN_MOTION`, `ECCENTRICITY`, `INCLINATION`, `RA_OF_ASC_NODE`, `ARG_OF_PERICENTER`, `MEAN_ANOMALY`, `NORAD_CAT_ID`, `BSTAR`, `MEAN_MOTION_DOT`, `MEAN_MOTION_DDOT`, `EPHEMERIS_TYPE`, `CLASSIFICATION_TYPE`

**Files.**

- `public/data/orbital/catalog.json` (8.68 MB, 35,652 records)

The GP/OMM element sets and SATCAT are "basic SSA data" originating from USSPACECOM (U.S. Space Force 18th/19th Space Defense Squadrons) via Space-Track.org, for which USSPACECOM grants "express blanket approval for transfer/redistribution of basic SSA data ... conditioned on appropriate citation" (Space-Track User Agreement, section "Redistribution of Basic SSA Information"). (<https://celestrak.org/usage-policy.php>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://celestrak.org/pub/satcat.csv>

No per-second limit documented (this pipeline waits 2.5 s between requests).

**Purpose.** Authoritative list of on-orbit objects (no decay date, Earth-centred): object class, owner, launch date/site, RCS, operational status, docking; orbit shape (apogee/perigee/inclination/period) for objects without GP elements; population statistics by class/regime/altitude shell.

**Mechanism.** HTTPS GET of the static full-catalog CSV -> filter DECAY_DATE empty and ORBIT_CENTER = EA (or docked to an Earth-orbiting host) -> joined with GP by NORAD_CAT_ID.

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/orbital/build.mjs

**Fallback.** Without SATCAT the app cannot show owner/class/launch metadata; render GP objects with class from name heuristics only and flag metadata as unavailable.

**Limitations.** SATCAT apogee/perigee/period/inclination are rounded (km, 0.01 deg/min) and can be stale for objects without current elements. RCS (m^2) is missing for ~58% of on-orbit objects (rcsSize null). OWNER is the SATCAT source code (country/organisation), not necessarily the operator. Analyst objects are not in SATCAT.

**Citation.** Orbital data: CelesTrak (Dr T.S. Kelso, https://celestrak.org) - GP element sets and SATCAT; source data: U.S. Space Force 18th & 19th Space Defense Squadrons / USSPACECOM via Space-Track.org.

<a id="sky-cmb"></a>
### Cosmic Microwave Background all-sky map — Planck PR3 (2018) SMICA CMB temperature map (foreground-cleaned)

- **Dataset id:** `sky-cmb`
- **Organization:** EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY. ALL RIGHTS RESERVED; HiPS by Buga M. (CDS)
- **Version:** HiPS CDS/P/PLANCK/R3/CMB released 2022-11-04T16:44Z (HiPS standard 1.4); Planck PR3 (2018) SMICA CMB temperature map (foreground-cleaned)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-18T14:17:28.120Z
- **License:** ESA Planck Legacy Archive data: CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO (ESA Space Science Archives terms; credit "ESA, Planck Collaboration"). HiPS: ODbL-1.0 (CDS). (<https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/esdc/terms-and-conditions>)
- **Provenance class:** derived
- **Endpoint:** <https://alasky.cds.unistra.fr/hips-image-services/hips2fits>
- **Update cadence:** static survey release (re-render only if CDS re-publishes the HiPS)
- **Rate limits:** hips2fits: not documented (max 50 million pixels per image; two independent endpoints alasky/alaskybis); MocServer: not documented. Cosmos throttles to >=1.1 s between requests per host, sequential, with retries/backoff.
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Cosmology finale (CMB sphere) and the Microwave/CMB mode of the Spectral View Switcher; numeric temperature read-outs.

**Mechanism.** CDS hips2fits service (HTTP GET, explicit CAR/ICRS WCS JSON) -> FITS -> sharp/Node normalisation -> JPEG/PNG/Float32; HiPS discovered via the CDS MocServer

**Query.**

```
GET https://alasky.cds.unistra.fr/hips-image-services/hips2fits?hips=CDS/P/PLANCK/R3/CMB&wcs={"NAXIS":2,"NAXIS1":4096,"NAXIS2":2048,"CTYPE1":"RA---CAR","CTYPE2":"DEC--CAR","CRPIX1":2048.5,"CRPIX2":1024.5,"CRVAL1":180,"CRVAL2":0,"CDELT1":0.087890625,"CDELT2":0.087890625,"CUNIT1":"deg","CUNIT2":"deg","RADESYS":"ICRS"}&format=fits
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/sky/fetch.mjs

**Fallback.** If missing, show the low-resolution preview (cmb_1k.jpg) or a labelled placeholder sphere; never synthesize a fake CMB pattern.

**Limitations.** Foreground-cleaned with the SMICA method; residual Galactic emission and point sources remain in a thin strip along the Galactic plane. The monopole (2.7255 K) and the dipole due to the Sun's motion (±3.36 mK) are removed; values are temperature differences in µK (K_CMB units). Effective resolution 5′ FWHM.

**Citation.** Based on observations obtained with Planck (http://www.esa.int/Planck), an ESA science mission with instruments and contributions directly funded by ESA Member States, NASA, and Canada. Credit: ESA, Planck Collaboration. Map: COM_CMB_IQU-smica_2048_R3.00_full (Planck Legacy Archive). HiPS: CDS. Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A4 (Planck 2018 results. IV. Diffuse component separation); Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A1. HiPS: Fernique et al. 2015, A&A 578, A114; reprojection: CDS hips2fits.

**Fields used (1).** `I_STOKES temperature (K_CMB) HiPS FITS tiles`

- **Organization:** This work is based on data from eROSITA, the soft X-ray instrument aboard SRG, a joint Russian-German science mission supported by the Russian Space Agency (Roskosmos), in the interests of the Russian Academy of Sciences represented by its Space Research Institute (IKI), and the Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR); HiPS by Jeremy Sanders, MPE
- **Version:** HiPS erosita/dr1/rate/rgb released 2024-01-31T11:00Z (HiPS standard 1.4); eROSITA-DE DR1 (eRASS1) RGB rate image: 0.2–0.5 keV (red), 0.5–1.0 keV (green), 1.0–2.0 keV (blue)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-18T14:40:30.915Z
- **License:** eROSITA-DE DR1 public data release (MPE, 2024-01-31); free use with the acknowledgement above. (<https://erosita.mpe.mpg.de/dr1/AllSkySurveyData_dr1/acknowledgement.html>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://alasky.cds.unistra.fr/hips-image-services/hips2fits>
- **Update cadence:** static survey release (re-render only if CDS re-publishes the HiPS)
- **Rate limits:** hips2fits: not documented (max 50 million pixels per image; two independent endpoints alasky/alaskybis); MocServer: not documented. Cosmos throttles to >=1.1 s between requests per host, sequential, with retries/backoff.
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Spectral View Switcher: real 0.2–2.0 keV (≈0.6–6 nm) all-sky texture for the celestial sphere (not recoloured visible light).

**Mechanism.** CDS hips2fits service (HTTP GET, explicit CAR/ICRS WCS JSON) -> PNG -> sharp/Node normalisation -> JPEG/PNG; HiPS discovered via the CDS MocServer

**Query.**

```
GET https://alasky.cds.unistra.fr/hips-image-services/hips2fits?hips=erosita/dr1/rate/rgb&wcs={"NAXIS":2,"NAXIS1":4096,"NAXIS2":2048,"CTYPE1":"RA---CAR","CTYPE2":"DEC--CAR","CRPIX1":2048.5,"CRPIX2":1024.5,"CRVAL1":180,"CRVAL2":0,"CDELT1":0.087890625,"CDELT2":0.087890625,"CUNIT1":"deg","CUNIT2":"deg","RADESYS":"ICRS"}&format=png
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/sky/fetch.mjs

**Fallback.** If missing, fall back to the 1024x512 preview; if that is missing too, hide this band in the switcher (do not recolour another band).

**Limitations.** Only the western Galactic hemisphere (Galactic longitude 180°–360°, the eROSITA-DE share) is public; the other half of the sky is black (no data) and flagged in the mask file.

**Citation.** This work is based on data from eROSITA, the soft X-ray instrument aboard SRG, a joint Russian-German science mission supported by the Russian Space Agency (Roskosmos), in the interests of the Russian Academy of Sciences represented by its Space Research Institute (IKI), and the Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR). The SRG spacecraft was built by Lavochkin Association (NPOL) and its subcontractors, and is operated by NPOL with support from the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics (MPE). HiPS: MPE (J. Sanders). Merloni A. et al. 2024, A&A 682, A34; Predehl P. et al. 2021, A&A 647, A1. HiPS: Fernique et al. 2015, A&A 578, A114; reprojection: CDS hips2fits.

**Fields used (1).** `RGB colour HiPS tiles (8-bit)`

- **Rate limits:** JPL SSD/CNEOS API Fair Use Policy: no numeric limit published; only one request at a time (no simultaneous requests); back off on errors; JPL may throttle or block unreasonable load. Scripts use sequential requests with >= 1.1 s spacing.

**Purpose.** Planetary-defense lab: upcoming asteroid/comet close approaches to Earth within 0.05 AU

**Mechanism.** REST API (JSON) -> compact table

**Query.**

```
date-min=2026-10-16&date-max=2036-10-16&dist-max=0.05&body=Earth&sort=date&diameter=true&fullname=true ; plus des=99942&date-min=2029-01-01&date-max=2029-12-31&dist-max=0.05&body=Earth&diameter=true&fullname=true
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/solar/fetch-cad.mjs

**Fallback.** Hide the close-approach list; Apophis 2029 record is also embedded in smallbodies.json notes.

**Limitations.** Predicted approaches change as orbits are refined; poorly observed objects have large distMin/distMax spread; diameter is measured only for a minority, otherwise null (H-based estimates are in neos.json).

**Citation.** NASA/JPL-Caltech Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS), SSD/CNEOS Close-Approach Data API.

- **Update cadence:** predicts are updated by flight dynamics teams after trajectory correction maneuvers
- **Rate limits:** JPL SSD/CNEOS API Fair Use Policy: no numeric limit published; only one request at a time (no simultaneous requests); back off on errors; JPL may throttle or block unreasonable load. Scripts use sequential requests with >= 1.1 s spacing.

**Purpose.** Spacecraft search and trajectories (Voyagers, New Horizons, Parker, Juno, Europa Clipper, Psyche, Lucy, Hera, JUICE, BepiColombo, JWST)

**Mechanism.** Horizons API EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS CSV (position only)

**Query.**

```
COMMAND=<naif>&CENTER=500@10 (JWST 500@399)&START_TIME=2025-01-01&STOP_TIME=2030-12-31&STEP_SIZE=<1|5> d&VEC_TABLE=1&REF_SYSTEM=ICRF&REF_PLANE=FRAME&OUT_UNITS=KM-S&TIME_TYPE=TDB&CSV_FORMAT=YES
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/solar/fetch-spacecraft.mjs

**Fallback.** Hide spacecraft whose track is missing; never extrapolate.

**Limitations.** Future portions are navigation predictions that shift after maneuvers; coarse steps for outer probes (5 d); Parker Solar Probe 1-day samples undersample perihelion passes. Mission status text is editorial and dated 2026-10; verify before presenting as current.

**Citation.** NASA/JPL Horizons On-Line Ephemeris System (https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/horizons/). Spacecraft trajectories from mission navigation teams via NAIF SPK kernels.

- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb_query.api>
- **Update cadence:** continuous (new discoveries daily)
- **Rate limits:** JPL SSD/CNEOS API Fair Use Policy: no numeric limit published; only one request at a time (no simultaneous requests); back off on errors; JPL may throttle or block unreasonable load. Scripts use sequential requests with >= 1.1 s spacing.

**Purpose.** Planetary-defense lab: orbits, sizes and MOIDs of potentially hazardous asteroids and the larger NEAs

**Mechanism.** SBDB Query API (two queries) -> JSON

**Query.**

```
fields=spkid,full_name,pdes,a,e,i,om,w,ma,epoch,tp,per,q,H,diameter,diameter_sigma,albedo,rot_per,moid,class,pha,condition_code,data_arc,n_obs_used,sigma_a,sigma_e,sigma_i,sigma_om,sigma_w,sigma_ma&full-prec=1&sb-kind=a&sb-group=pha  +  fields=spkid,full_name,pdes,a,e,i,om,w,ma,epoch,tp,per,q,H,diameter,diameter_sigma,albedo,rot_per,moid,class,pha,condition_code,data_arc,n_obs_used,sigma_a,sigma_e,sigma_i,sigma_om,sigma_w,sigma_ma&full-prec=1&sb-kind=a&sb-group=neo&sb-cdata={"AND":["H|LT|18"]}
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/solar/fetch-neos.mjs

**Fallback.** Hide the NEO table; keep notable bodies from smallbodies.json.

**Limitations.** diameterEstKm is a rough H-based estimate (real albedos span ~0.03-0.5, so diameters are uncertain by about a factor of 2); only a minority have measured diameters. Osculating elements; not a complete NEO catalog (H<18 plus PHAs).

**Citation.** NASA/JPL Solar System Dynamics and CNEOS, Small-Body Database Query API.

**Fields used (30).** `spkid`, `full_name`, `pdes`, `a`, `e`, `i`, `om`, `w`, `ma`, `epoch`, `tp`, `per`, `q`, `H`, `diameter`, `diameter_sigma`, `albedo`, `rot_per`, `moid`, `class`, `pha`, `condition_code`, `data_arc`, `n_obs_used`, `sigma_a`, `sigma_e`, `sigma_i`, `sigma_om`, `sigma_w`, `sigma_ma`

<a id="constellation-figures-boundaries"></a>
### IAU constellation lines (Stellarium modern_iau) and boundaries (VizieR VI/49)

- **Dataset id:** `constellation-figures-boundaries`
- **Organization:** Stellarium team; CDS / Davenhall & Leggett (Delporte 1930)
- **Version:** Stellarium commit dc5679c; VI/49 VizieR VI/49, CDS ReadMe history last entry 23-Jul-2024 (J2000 boundaries for CEP and UMI fixed.)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-17T06:15:27.293Z
- **License:** Lines: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Stellarium modern_iau). Boundaries: CDS VizieR open data, cite catalogue. (<https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/>)
- **Provenance class:** reconstructed
- **Endpoint:** <https://github.com/Stellarium/stellarium/blob/dc5679c9723685585196c4d6ecd7ffd33da59ecd/skycultures/modern_iau/index.json ; https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/ftp/VI/49/constbnd.dat>
- **Update cadence:** static (boundaries 1930; figures change rarely)
- **Rate limits:** not documented
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Constellation figures that distort in 3-D, labels and sky-area boundaries

**Mechanism.** raw GitHub JSON (pinned commit) + CDS FTP flat files -> Node build (B1875 boundaries precessed to J2000, densified to 1 deg)

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/stars/build.mjs

**Fallback.** Hide constellation overlay

**Limitations.** Figures are a cultural convention (one of several). 1 segment (UMa, HIP 55203) has an endpoint absent from HYG and 18 other endpoints lack parallax (no 3-D position; use lineStars RA/Dec). Boundaries reconstructed: B1875 edges precessed to J2000 and sampled at 1 deg; all 12,948 VI/49 J2000 vertices lie within 7.6 arcsec of them.

**Citation.** Constellation figures: Stellarium sky culture "modern_iau" (Stellarium team; figures after the IAU / Sky & Telescope constellation charts by Roger Sinnott, Rick Fienberg and Alan MacRobert), CC BY-SA 4.0, https://github.com/Stellarium/stellarium. Constellation boundaries: Davenhall A.C., Leggett S.K. 1989, "Catalogue of Constellation Boundary Data", CDS VizieR VI/49 (1997yCat.6049....0D), after Delporte E. 1930, "Delimitation scientifique des constellations". This research has made use of the VizieR catalogue access tool, CDS, Strasbourg, France (DOI: 10.26093/cds/vizier).

**Fields used (5).** `lines (HIP pairs)`, `RAhr`, `DEdeg`, `cst`, `adj`

### Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars (GCNS, EDR3, <=100 pc)

- **Dataset id:** `gaia-gcns-100pc`
- **Organization:** ESA Gaia DPAC (Smart et al. 2021)
- **Version:** Gaia EDR3 (GCNS table external.gaiaedr3_gcns_main_1)
- **Retrieved:** 2026-10-18T17:44:45.107Z
- **License:** ESA Gaia data licence: CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO (non-commercial, educational exhibition use) (<https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia-users/license>)
- **Provenance class:** observed
- **Endpoint:** <https://gea.esac.esa.int/tap-server/tap>
- **Update cadence:** Gaia DR4 due 2026-12-02 (NOT used); EDR3 static
- **Rate limits:** anonymous async jobs capped at 50,000 rows per job (hence band splitting)
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Catalog-adapter demo: complete 100 pc volume with HR-diagram colours

**Mechanism.** ESA Gaia Archive TAP async ADQL (24 RA bands) -> CSV -> Float32 binary

**Query.**

```
SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_error, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, dist_16, dist_50, dist_84, gcns_prob, wd_prob, ruwe FROM external.gaiaedr3_gcns_main_1 WHERE ra >= a AND ra < b (24 bands of 15 deg)
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/stars/fetch-gcns.mjs + build-gcns.mjs

**Fallback.** Use HYG field only

**Limitations.** Positions at epoch J2016.0, not propagated. 431 rows lack G (dropped); 6,574 lack BP-RP (NaN). Distances are GCNS Bayesian medians. Contains faint dwarfs to G~21.

**Citation.** Gaia Collaboration, Smart R.L., Sarro L.M., et al. 2021, "Gaia Early Data Release 3: The Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars", A&A 649, A6 (doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202039498). Credit: ESA/Gaia/DPAC. This work has made use of data from the European Space Agency (ESA) mission Gaia (https://www.cosmos.esa.int/gaia), processed by the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC, https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/gaia/dpac/consortium). Funding for the DPAC has been provided by national institutions, in particular the institutions participating in the Gaia Multilateral Agreement.

- **Endpoint:** <https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/thredds/dodsC/global/ETOPO2022/60s/60s_surface_elev_netcdf/ETOPO_2022_v1_60s_N90W180_surface.nc>
- **Update cadence:** static archive products (rarely updated)
- **Rate limits:** not documented
- **Cache policy:** versioned offline snapshot; optional online refresh

**Purpose.** Earth specular (ocean) mask, height/bump and normal map

**Mechanism.** OPeNDAP .dods (z[lat][lon], stride 2 = 10800x5400) -> area resample -> derived maps

**Query.**

```
z.z[0:2:10798][0:2:21598] in 6 latitude chunks
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/textures/build-earth.mjs

**Fallback.** Use a flat albedo colour per body (see index.json) and keep the scene running; never fetch online during the exhibition

**Limitations.** Stride-2 subsample of the 60" grid (~3.7 km); normal slope exaggerated x6; ocean mask = z<0 (includes Caspian/Dead Sea depressions); bathymetry not used for normals.

**Citation.** NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information. 2022: ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model. doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74

**Purpose.** Global surface maps: Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus surface, Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto, Titan, Enceladus, Triton, Pluto, Charon

**Mechanism.** OGC WMS 1.1.1 GetMap EPSG:4326 4096x2048 PNG

**Query.**

```
see per-body endpoint in index.json credits / records
```

**Normalization script.** scripts/data/textures/build-wms.mjs

**Fallback.** Use a flat albedo colour per body (see index.json) and keep the scene running; never fetch online during the exhibition

**Limitations.** Server-resampled; Pluto/Charon/Triton far sides unobserved and Europa/Ganymede/Callisto polar gaps are filled with smooth interpolation (illustrative); Moon/Mercury/Pluto/Charon/Enceladus are greyscale; Venus colour is artificial; Moon has no bump map in this build. Moon/Mars normal maps are derived from 8-bit grey elevation stretches (approximate heights). Triton/Pluto/Charon unobserved regions are faded to mean colour; coverage masks provided.

**Citation.** USGS Astrogeology Science Center / NASA mission teams (see credits in index.json)
